newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends lower on seedings, CBOT.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends lower on seedings, CBOT.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures closed lower on active seedings of the U.S. spring wheat crop and on a sharp drop in Chicago grain and soybean futures, traders said.
"We declined along with Chicago and bearish planting numbers came out yesterday," a trader said.
USDA said 59 percent of the spring wheat crop had been seeded as of Sunday, ahead of the 45-percent-planted figure a year ago but behind the 70 percent average pace.
"We had scattered selling among four or five different firms," the trader said.
Benson Quinn, Wilson Trading, LFG Futures and General Mills were the key sellers of the July contract, traders said.
The May contract expired at 1201 CDT and was unchanged at $4.26 per bushel.
MGE spring wheat futures closed unchanged to 12-1/4 cents per bushel lower, with July down 12-1/4 at $4.02-1/2 a bushel.
MGE barley futures closed unchanged to $0.10 per cwt higher, with May expiring up $0.10 at $6.90 per cwt. July closed unchanged at $6.70 per cwt.
Spring wheat futures volume was estimated by the MGE at 20.331 million bushels versus actual volume Monday of 10.754.
